column12: Judgement on the comparator. Osavampator's Phase 3 setting is the adjunctive-MDD slot, and Vraylar is labelled 'adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adult patients' (book labels table, Vraylar SPL v32). The only Vraylar efficacy supplement between 2019 and 2025 is dated 2022-12-16 (book supplements table, NDA204370 s9, openFDA). I take it to be the MDD approval, but the table does not name the indication. If so, Vraylar's 2024 Medicare spend includes MDD use, which Caplyta's (MDD label November 2025, per the seltorexant seed) does not. It is also the book's anchor for brenipatide in the same disease, so the two price alike. Rexulti, the other branded adjunctive-MDD atypical, has no row in the book's CMS table. Cross-checks, Part D 2024 (lookup.py demand): Caplyta $9,940 (the seltorexant anchor, 3% higher), Auvelity $4,686, Spravato $23,121. The case against: Vraylar's Medicare spend is mostly schizophrenia and bipolar use. A beneficiary's spend covers about 198 days of therapy (23,309,776 dosage units over 117,573 beneficiaries), so it understates an annual price. Auvelity, the newest MDD-only brand and also glutamatergic, sells for half as much, and payers can put generic aripiprazole and quetiapine first. Vraylar's own Medicare price is negotiated from 2027 (see gross_to_net_pct). No price for osavampator has been published, since it is not approved

column12: Judgement: reused from the closest modelled competitor, an oral once-daily add-on in the same adjunctive-MDD setting, over a 24-week window. Osavampator's own data are shorter. In SAVITRI, 161 of 183 randomised (88%) completed 8 weeks of treatment, all arms pooled (Psych Congress 2025 poster 33, hmpgloballearningnetwork.com/node/371481, read from a search summary, page not opened). Annualised at a constant hazard, 1 - 0.88^(365.25/56) = 0.566, which is the case for lower. It was not used because 8 weeks is extrapolated six-fold and the pool includes the placebo half. Also for lower: in MarketScan, 19% of patients on an adjunctive atypical antipsychotic discontinued, against 42% on monotherapy (Jain et al., Drugs Real World Outcomes 2022;9(3):477-486, doi:10.1007/s40801-022-00316-4, PMID 35771409; abstract gives no time window, so not annualised). The case for higher: trial retention usually beats real-world persistence on antidepressant add-ons

column12: Judgement on the timeline. No NDA date has been published (searched). Topline in the second half of 2027, an NDA in the first half of 2028 and a standard review for a new molecular entity put US approval in the first half of 2029, so 2030 is the first full year. The seltorexant seed runs from a December 2026 primary completion to a first full year of 2029; the same steps from July 2027 land in 2030. The case for earlier: an approval early in 2029 gives most of 2029 on the market. The case for later: if FDA wants the maintenance study (2028-07) in the filing, or the safety database waits on NCT06966401, approval slips to 2030 and the first full year to 2031

column11: Three filters, applied to the NSDUH past-year MDE pool. (1) Treated: 61.0% of US adults with a past-year MDE received treatment (NIMH, nimh.nih.gov/health/statistics/major-depression, NSDUH 2021), the book's brenipatide and seltorexant value. (2) Moderate or severe: the Phase 3 enrols 'recurrent MDD (moderate or severe) or persistent depressive disorder' (NCT06786624 key inclusion criteria, clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06786624, via search). Of 12-month MDD cases in the NCS-R, 10.4% were mild, 38.6% moderate, 38.0% severe and 12.9% very severe on the QIDS-SR, so 89.5% were moderate or worse (Kessler et al., JAMA 2003;289(23):3095-3105, doi:10.1001/jama.289.23.3095, PMID 12813115). (3) Inadequate response to an antidepressant in the current episode (NCT06786624 inclusion): 47% responded to citalopram in STAR*D level 1 among 2,876 US outpatients, so 53% did not (Trivedi et al., Am J Psychiatry 2006;163:28-40, doi:10.1176/appi.ajp.163.1.28, PMID 16390886), the seltorexant seed's value. 0.61 x 0.895 x 0.53 = 0.289354
column12: Judgement: the filters are taken as independent. The label pool is about 6.20mm US adults (21,414,000 x 0.289354). Cross-check: Neurocrine says 'approximately one-third of over 16 million people in the U.S. who live with MDD do not achieve adequate relief with existing antidepressants' (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007), about 5.3mm. Not applied: the trial's 'recurrent' criterion, because adjunctive-MDD labels are written for MDD without that limit (Vraylar: 'adjunctive therapy to antidepressants for the treatment of major depressive disorder (MDD) in adult patients', book labels table). That is the case for lower: a label that kept 'recurrent' would cut the pool further. The case for higher: treated patients skew more severe than all 12-month cases, so filter (2) understates. STAR*D level 1 already required moderate or worse depression (HRSD 14 or more). The trial also admits persistent depressive disorder, which lies outside this pool. 'Treated' includes talk therapy alone, while the label needs an ongoing antidepressant. The seltorexant label (0.19398 of the pool, with an insomnia filter) sits largely inside this one, so the two compete for the same patients

column12: Judgement: a 1.0x multiple on Auvelity, the newest oral MDD brand with a clean CMS series and, like osavampator, a glutamatergic mechanism. It applies the rate Auvelity took of its own label pool (all diagnosed depression) to osavampator's narrower pool: 21,414,000 x 0.289354 x 0.001417 = about 8,780 new patients a year at peak. The case for higher: only 2% of 455,082 newly diagnosed MDD patients in MarketScan received an adjunctive atypical antipsychotic regimen in the study window (Jain et al. 2022, PMID 35771409), which leaves room for an add-on without the metabolic and movement side effects of that class. SAVITRI reported no dissociation or sedation (search summary of the Psych Congress 2025 poster). Neurocrine already sells INGREZZA to psychiatrists. 2024 was also Auvelity's second full year, not its peak. The case for lower: a first-in-class mechanism with only a 183-patient Phase 2 behind it, cheap generic aripiprazole and quetiapine in the slot, and seltorexant and brenipatide competing for the same add-on patients

column12: Judgement on the comparator. Neurocrine keeps osavampator's rights everywhere except Japan (10-Q 0000914475-26-000037), but has no filed ex-US split of its own: it sells INGREZZA 'exclusively in the U.S.' and licenses Asia to Tanabe for a royalty (FY2025 10-K 0000914475-26-000007). Spravato is the book's measured split for a depression brand, and the closest modelled competitor uses it. The case for lower, and it is strong: Neurocrine has no ex-US sales force, and the adjunctive-MDD brands book almost nothing abroad. Vraylar shows $9mm international against $3,612mm US in FY2025 (book asset_revenue_regions, AbbVie annual report table 0001551152-26-000008), because Gedeon Richter sells it outside the US, and Caplyta shows $0 against $700mm. If Neurocrine licenses ex-US rights out, it earns a royalty, not sales. The case for higher: the Takeda agreement sets an ex-US royalty rate, which suggests ex-US sales are planned, and an oral pill is easier to launch abroad than an in-clinic spray
